To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Cluster observations at high altitudes are consistent with a quasi-stationnary generator electric field; (ii) the energy spectrum of the electrons precipitating in the ionosphere is in agreement with the optical observations of polar caps arcs by TIMED.

the polar cap arc and the associated ion upflowing beams are the result of a quasi-static process in which a generator electric field accelerates electrons that are subsequently precipitated in the ionosphere and produce the optical emission.

(1) the polar cap ion upflows and the polar cap arcs are related to the same process; (2) the polar cap arcs and ion upflows are signatures of quasi-static acceleration and precipitation of magnetospheric electrons; (3) the polar cap arc is a large scale phenomenon that can be modelled using Cluster observations of upflows at high altitude; and (4) the polar cap upflows and arc are related to the configuration of the magnetosphere during prolonged Northward IMF
